messages.author: 4a5459c655bd0648
messages.subject: Correlating residuals of indicators
parts:
Hi,

I have a simple one-factor model of a latent construct composed of 10 individual indicators. As all indicators are supposed to measure the same thing I wonder whether we should not always - by default - assume that their residuals covary? Are there any downsides of specifying this in my model (other than taking away some dfs)? 

Then I am wondering whether there is an easy (and quick) way to specify that all residuals covary with each other?

I tried the below command but it didn't work. 
# residual (co)variances
    y1 + y2 = y3... ~~ y1 = y2 ....

messages.author: 99a06696c483481a
messages.subject: Re: Correlating residuals of indicators
parts: A common factor is not a composite. If it were, then your strategy would make sense, but it is not. You cannot allow all free residual covariances and estimate a factor model. The factor is constructed out of the covariances among the observed variables--the factor "explains" and "accounts for" these covariances, because all the observed variables are jointly dependent on the factor. If all residual covariances are free, there is nothing for the common factor to explain, and statistical identification will fail. The principle of "conditional independence" states that, if the common factor model is strictly correct, then the residuals for the observed variables will be uncorrelated, because all of their shared variance has been accounted for by the factor. Any good text on factor analysis should make these points.

messages.subject: Re: Correlating residuals of indicators
parts:
Hi,

You are not taking away “some dfs” by doing that, but taking away all dfs, which makes the model underidentified  and as a consequence, you would not be able to meaningfully estimate it.

Mikko
